_comment: Instance data for core/helpers/autonomous-mode.cjs: regex strings in the operator's own language that
ORDER an autonomous run (on_patterns), end it (off_patterns), or answer yes to 'continue autonomously?'
(yes_patterns). The built-ins are English ('autonomous', 'work the list alone', 'I'm away' / 'normal mode',
'stop autonomous' / 'yes'). The mode is a latch: an on-word sets it, an off-word clears it, and so does a
prompt that asks what is open (the ask_patterns of open-items.json - the operator who asks is here); a yes
to a question-tool question carrying an on-word sets it again. Anything else ('status?', a remark) keeps it.
Example for a German operator: on "\\bautonom", "\\ballein abarbeiten\\b", "\\bich bin weg\\b";
off "\\bnormalmodus\\b", "\\bnicht mehr autonom\\b"; yes "^\\s*ja\\b". Read by autonomous-gate
(no question tool, no ask dialog in the mode), stoppen-gate and open-items-gate.
_cases: the operator's real wording with the mode the latch must reach (steps = prompts in order, {q, a} =
a question-tool answer); run through autonomous-mode.cjs by core/scripts/pattern-cases.py at every
self-test. Replace the English examples with the operator's own words, the answer path included.
statusline_labels (optional): the words helpers/statusline.cjs shows for the mode, e.g.
INTERACTIVE. `help` (a project path or a URL) makes the word a Cmd/Ctrl+click link to a page explaining the mode.
